messages.author: f2a74e4c4c138715
messages.subject: Plotting variograms
parts:
Hello, Im trying to create a facet plot of the variograms from each animal used in my study to show range residency. I'm not very familiar with base R plotting language which is what CTMM graphics seems to be built around. Hence Im trying to use the raw SVF files as general dataframes with SVF, DOF, and lag values to plot in ggplot (i.e. facet_wrap).

I see the lag values are in seconds which I can use to limit the x axis for a zoomed in plot of e.g. two month lag to show curve / assymptote. The problem is replicating the SVF values with 95% CI on the y axis. 

What unit is the SVF column in? Is it m2? Also how I can use the DOF values to show 95% confidence interval?

Any general advice on how folks are customising their outputs from the CTMM package for publication worthy plots would be much appreciated. 

Thank you, much appreciated.
Chris

messages.author: 40fd627580dd34f5
messages.subject: Re: Plotting variograms
parts:
Hi Chris,

For a facet-style plot in base plot, I usually just adjust par(mfrow).

The units on most all plots and summaries are automated for readability unless units=FALSE. The SVF y-axis could be in m^2, hectares, or km^2 depending on the size of the numbers.
With the plots, I store the units information in ctmm:::plot.env and apply the %#% unit conversion operator to anything that I want to plot atop that.

Best,
Chris
